output.review_comment:
Splitting over-long words into width-sized chunks and returning `[]` for empty or whitespace-only input both look like reasonable fixes. The problem is the comparison change from `<= width` to `< width` when joining words.

With that change, a line built from two or more words can be at most `width - 1` characters. A single word, or a chunk of a split word, can still be exactly `width` characters. So the same limit is applied two different ways. For example, `wrap_text("ab cd", 5)` now returns `["ab", "cd"]`, even though "ab cd" is exactly 5 characters and fits. That breaks the plain meaning of `width` as the maximum line length, and the docstring is supposed to be the source of truth here. This looks like an off-by-one tweak made to get a particular test to pass, not a fix to the actual logic.

The PR has no description, so nothing explains why this change is correct or which test needed it. Please either:
- revert to `<=` and find the real cause of the failing test, or
- quote the docstring wording that says joined lines must be strictly shorter than `width`, and then make single words and chunks follow the same rule.

Also add a short description saying which tests were failing and why.
